messages:
customer_acmecorp: Hey team — we started seeing a bunch of streaming responses from the API that cut off mid-output, then the client reconnects and we get the tail tokens again (duplicates). Happening ~10% of streaming calls for one service. No obvious 5xx. Started after we rolled proxy change last night.

maya_support: Thanks for the report — can you paste a short repro (curl or client snippet) + any request IDs if you have them? Also which endpoint (chat/streaming or gen/streaming)?

customer_acmecorp: It's chat streaming via /v1/chat/stream. Quick repro I used locally: 

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-stream","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"explain quantum tunneling"}]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```

I attached one server request-id: req_44a7f8c2 and a client trace id trace-7b.

sam_engineering: Noted. Two quick hypotheses: (1) ALB / TLS-proxy idle timeout is closing the TCP but client sees the SSE stream cut (2) our runtime emits SSE comment pings ": ping" which some proxies strip and consider as idle traffic — that can reset idle timers incorrectly.

alex_oncall: Adding logs from runtime around req_44a7f8c2 — we see: 

```
[2026-03-14T18:02:12Z] req=44a7f8c2 stream-start model=redwood-1-stream client=trace-7b
[2026-03-14T18:02:13Z] req=44a7f8c2 chunk token_count=12
[2026-03-14T18:02:15Z] req=44a7f8c2 keepalive: sent comment-ping
[2026-03-14T18:02:20Z] req=44a7f8c2 tcp-reset by upstream (FIN)
[2026-03-14T18:02:20Z] req=44a7f8c2 conn-closed reason=tls-session-idle
[2026-03-14T18:02:20Z] req=44a7f8c2 stream-finalized state=partial
```

maya_support: That tcp-reset + tls-session-idle sounds like a proxy/ALB timed out the TLS session. Which proxy did AcmeCorp use?

customer_acmecorp: We're on internal infra using Envoy in front of a TLS-terminating NGINX that then connects to the redwood private endpoint (customer-managed). We rolled an Envoy config last night to change http/2 settings.

kevin_infra: Envoy + NGINX layering is a classic caveat. Two relevant knobs: upstream idle timeout (tcp_keepalive vs app-level pings) and whether the proxy treats SSE comment lines as traffic. Some proxies ignore colon comments when computing idle. If the runtime only sends comment pings, the proxy might still tear down.

sam_engineering: Workable next steps: 
- get tcpdump/tcp_keepalive stats to confirm final FIN sequence (we already see tcp-reset log).
- try switching to explicit SSE `event: ping\ndata: {"now":123}\n\n` (i.e., application-level event frames) so intermediaries see longer payloads.
- as a mitigation, increase upstream idle timeout to 60s or enable TLS session keepalive at proxy.

maya_support: Customer, can you do a quick test: set Envoy upstream idle_timeout to 90s and repro one call? If you can't, we can try toggling runtime to send event pings instead of comment pings for your tenant as a short-term workaround.

customer_acmecorp: We have a maintenance window in 30m so we can flip the envoy setting. I'll try and report back.

deploy-bot: deploy status: envoy-config/edge-v2 -> deployed by julie_ops @ 2026-03-14T18:22:10Z :white_check_mark:

customer_acmecorp: OK changed idle_timeout to 90s on upstream, re-ran the curl repro 20 times. No disconnects in 20 runs. Before change ~2/20 had partials.

sam_engineering: Nice. That points to proxy idle. We should still add an option to runtime to emit a small event payload every 15s rather than `: comment` to be robust across proxies.

alex_oncall: Agreed. Adding engineering tasks: 
- runtime: new config `sse.keepalive_mode: event|comment|none` (default comment for minimal bytes)
- infra-docs: guidance for envoys/nginx that treat colon comments as idle.
- support KB: troubleshooting steps + curl repro snippet.

kevin_infra: Small note: switching to `event` increases bytes on high-throughput tenants — we should measure cost impact vs reliability. But for now, tenant-specific override is fine.

maya_support: Customer — we'll provision a tenant override to `event` for your project if you prefer. That should avoid intermediate proxies dropping sessions even with default timeouts. Do you want us to enable?

customer_acmecorp: Yes please enable event-mode for our tenant. Also can you add a header we can watch in logs to correlate reconnects? Something like `x-rw-stream-id` echoed?

sam_engineering: We can add an `X-RW-STREAM-ID` header on the response lines for correlation — server will include it in initial response and logs. Implementation note: can't add header mid-stream (SSE) but the initial response headers will include it and we can also include it in the payload as `event: meta\ndata: {"stream_id":".."}\n\n`.

alex_oncall: I'll enable `event` mode for tenant acmecorp-123 and add the correlation event. Will follow up once toggled.

deploy-bot: feature-flag change: sse_event_mode=on for tenant=acmecorp-123 applied by alex_oncall @ 2026-03-14T18:51:02Z :white_check_mark:

customer_acmecorp: After toggle we ran the same curl test 50x — zero disconnects, no duplicates. Thanks! We'll keep monitoring.

maya_support: Great. Follow-ups: 
- sam/eng: propose default change to `event` if more than X% of endpoints report proxy disconnect patterns? Or leave default as comment but stronger documentation?
- kevin: add sample Envoy + NGINX snippets in infra docs for idle_timeout and tcp_keepalive.

sam_engineering: My preference: keep default `comment` (smaller bytes) but add auto-detect heuristics: if we see frequent TLS session idle closes + partial state, flip to `event` per-tenant automatically with alert to support. For now that's a P2.

kevin_infra: I'll draft the Envoy doc today and include recommended values: idle_timeout >= 60s, `use_remote_address`, and keep TLS session resumption settings.

maya_support: Customer — closing the ticket in our tracker but leaving monitoring alerts for 24h. If you see regressions ping here and we can revert/adjust. Thanks for quick repro info and patience. :pray:

customer_acmecorp: Appreciate the fast turnaround. One last ask — will this cause any billing impact? More bytes from `event` pings?

sam_engineering: Minimal. The event payload is ~20–40 bytes every 15s per open stream. On typical session lengths it's negligible compared to tokens. We'll add a note to billing KB.

maya_support: Closing thread — marked resolved.
